rejection_reason: Parked (not dropped). The registry blocker is now ANSWERED, and what remains is one bounded worker pull plus the split/base-rate measurements. Measured 2026-09-23: a facility roster that is independent of the overflow reports does exist - EPA's ICIS-NPDES 'ICIS_FACILITIES.csv' ships in https://echo.epa.gov/files/echodownloads/npdes_downloads.zip (352,268,538 bytes, anonymous, supports byte ranges, member ICIS_FACILITIES.csv 193,927,778 bytes uncompressed / 71,317,447 compressed; documented fields NPDES_ID, FACILITY_UIN, FACILITY_TYPE_CODE, CITY, COUNTY_CODE, STATE_CODE, lat/long on EPA's ICIS-NPDES download summary page). Maryland's own portal also carries rosters, but each is a SUBSET and was measured as such: 'Significant Wastewater Treatment Plants' (2h5v-duyx and its duplicate ct9h-nxwr) is 76 distinct NPDES IDs, all Major POTWs - 40 of them appear in the reports, 36 never report in either series; 'Point Source Discharges' (wdtu-5pbn / rwxr-95kt, 863 rows, 829 distinct NPDES IDs, permit categories including 184 Waste Water Treatment Plant, 63 Publically Owned Treatment Waste Water, 2 Combined Sewer Overflow, 39 Stormwater Discharge) covers only 129 of the reports' 322 distinct NPDES IDs. Neither Maryland roster is therefore exhaustive. Remaining blocker: pull ICIS_FACILITIES.csv, filter STATE_CODE=MD, and measure how many of the reports' 322 distinct NPDES IDs it covers and whether it distinguishes collection systems from industrial outfalls; until that is measured a facility-day grid cannot be asserted to be complete. Also still open: the 2023 row-level reconciliation and the split/base-rate counts (the only amount measured so far is 322 distinct reporting NPDES IDs, 126 in the old series and 247 in the new, and 1,024 reports attributable to the 76-facility major-POTW roster).

novelty_check.theirs: EPA publishes the raw ICIS-NPDES files and MDE publishes the overflow reports and partial rosters; neither ships the joined facility-day task, its temporal splits or a scored contract. Prior art models citywide CSO from internal utility telemetry (DeepCSO) and open GitHub code (tbep-tech/sso-dash, HamedGhodsi90/CSO_Real-Time_Prediction, AlexLipp/cso_scaling) - no ML-ready dataset with splits.
novelty_check.ours: A facility-day prediction task over Maryland collection systems: the roster comes from an independent permit registry (EPA ICIS-NPDES facility file; MDE's own inventories are partial and measured as such), so facilities that never reported are rows in the grid rather than absent; features are rainfall (GHCN-Daily access CSVs, tokenless) and facility identity; positives are the two MDE public-domain reported-overflow series, abutting in 2023.
novelty_check.rule: A dataset that already exists in ML-ready form is not published. Mirroring is a failure mode, not a contribution.
